sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH (2020)
cleanIntro: Traditions asks for this after every shooting session. The NitroFire is the odd one in this family: there is no removable breech plug, because the Firestick seals the chamber. The strip stops at barrel-off-frame, and the barrel carries a shelf the Firestick seats against that only a brush may cross.

steps.title: Treat it as loaded
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and handle it as a loaded gun.
steps.quote: WARNING: ALWAYS POINT THE NITROFIRE™ IN A SAFE DIRECTION AND TREAT THE NITROFIRE™ AS IF IT WAS LOADED AND CAN FIRE. WARNING: CONFIRM THE NITROFIRE™ IS UNLOADED BEFORE CONDUCTING ANY OF THE METHODS IN THIS SECTION.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: De-cock before you try to open it
steps.action: At full cock the action is locked shut. Thumb the hammer, press the trigger, and ride it down to rest.
steps.quote: NOTE: When the NitroFire™ is in the full cock position, the action is locked in battery and cannot be opened. If your NitroFire™ is in the full cock position and you no longer want to fire the NitroFire™, carefully follow these steps to de-cock the firearm. Unloading can be accomplished into the At Rest position. Once the hammer is in this position, engage the manual trigger safety. Follow the directions below: 1. Both hands should be dry and not impeded in any way. 2. Disengage the manual trigger safety by pressing the button from right to left so the red ring is visible. WARNING: THE FIREARM IS NO LONGER IN THE "SAFE" POSITION. 3. Carefully, while holding your thumb on the hammer in the cocked position, depress the trigger slowly until you feel the hammer release. Immediately release your finger from the trigger and slowly lower the hammer in a controlled manner into the At Rest position. Engage the manual trigger safety so the red ring is no longer visible. At this point you can safely open the action.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 14 De-cocking the NitroFire — p.30
steps.warn: Never dry fire the NitroFire. Lower the hammer under thumb control.

steps.title: Remove the Firestick
steps.action: Open the action and lift the Firestick out with your fingers. The charge lives in the Firestick, not in the barrel.
steps.prose: This is what makes the NitroFire different from a conventional muzzleloader: pulling the Firestick removes the powder charge in one piece. A bullet may still be seated ahead of the shelf.
steps.quote: 2. Open the action and carefully remove the Firestick™ with your fingers. Close the action.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 15 Unloading the NitroFire If You Don't Fire — p.31

steps.title: Engage the safety
steps.action: Push the safety across until the red ring disappears.
steps.quote: 1. Follow all safety rules listed previously in this manual. Be sure the safety is engaged so it is in the "safe" position and the red ring is not visible.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: Open and inspect, then close the action
steps.action: Depress the barrel catch lever, check the barrel is unprimed, unloaded and clear, then close it again.
steps.quote: 2. Open the NitroFire™ by depressing the barrel catch lever. Inspect the barrel to be sure your NitroFire™ is unprimed, unloaded, and free of obstruction. Once you've determined the NitroFire™ is safe you can close the action.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Pull the ramrod out of the thimbles and set it aside.
steps.quote: 3. Remove the ramrod from the NitroFire™.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: Remove the forend screw
steps.action: Back the forend stock screw out of the barrel assembly with the 4mm Allen wrench.
steps.quote: 4. Remove the forend stock screw from the barrel assembly using the 4mm Allen wrench.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.35

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Push the catch lever in and lift the barrel out of the frame. Barrel and frame are the two pieces you clean — there is no breech plug to remove.
steps.prose: Every other Traditions break-open in this catalog has a removable breech plug at this point. The NitroFire does not: the Firestick seals the chamber, so the strip stops at barrel-off-frame.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the barrel from the frame by pushing the barrel catch lever in. 6. When the barrel starts to open, lift the barrel out of the frame. You can now clean your barrel and frame. Field disassembly is now complete.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.35

steps.title: Wet the bore and let the solvent work
steps.action: Charge the bore brush with solvent and let it sit in the barrel before scrubbing.
steps.quote: 3. Spray a bore solvent, such as Traditions™ BlackOut 209 solvent, on your bore brush. Note: Traditions™ Foaming Bore Solvent can also be used instead of spraying the bore solvent on the bronze brush. Allow solvent to sit for 15 minutes inside the barrel. This will allow time for the solvent to engage and penetrate the fouling. Do not let it dry.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.35

steps.title: Scrub past the shelf with the bronze brush
steps.action: Push the bronze brush from the breech out through the muzzle and draw it back. The brush is the one tool allowed past the shelf.
steps.aside: The shelf is the step in the bore the Firestick seats against. Only the brush crosses it; patches must not.
steps.quote: 4. To clean your barrel, insert your bronze brush into the breech area. Push the ramrod from the breech to the muzzle until the brush exits the muzzle. Pull the ramrod back through the barrel towards the breech. The technique allows you to go past the shelf in the barrel and helps to break up fouling.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.36

steps.title: Patch from the muzzle down to the shelf
steps.action: Run dry patches from the muzzle and stop at the shelf. Repeat until they come out clean.
steps.quote: 6. Place a dry cotton patch over the jag and insert it into the muzzle. Run the ramrod with the patch from the muzzle to the shelf in the barrel to help remove fouling. Pull the ramrod back through to the muzzle. Repeat until patch comes out clean. WARNING: Do not push past the barrel shelf.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.36
steps.warn: Do not push a patch past the barrel shelf. A patch driven past it can lodge where the Firestick has to seat.

steps.title: Clean the chamber up to the back of the shelf
steps.action: Work the nylon brush into the chamber as far as the back of the shelf and out again.
steps.prose: Both faces of the shelf have to be clean or the Firestick will not seat fully — which is the whole reason the manual keeps returning to it.
steps.quote: 7. To clean the chamber area, spray the NitroFire™ Nylon Bore Brush with the bore solvent and insert it into the chamber up to the back of the shelf. Pull the brush back out of the chamber. You may feel some resistance. Repeat this process until the chamber area and back of the shelf is clean.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.36

deepSteps.title: Dry-patch the chamber to the shelf
deepSteps.action: Push dry patches from the breech opening up to the shelf until they come out clean.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Place a dry cotton patch over the cleaning jag and insert it into the chamber. Carefully push the ramrod with the patch from the breech opening to the barrel shelf. Repeat until patch comes out clean. WARNING: Do not push past the barrel shelf.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.36
deepSteps.warn: Do not push past the barrel shelf.

deepSteps.title: Season the bore from the muzzle
deepSteps.action: Push a seasoning or lubed patch from the muzzle down to the shelf and stop there.
deepSteps.quote: 9. Using a Traditions™ Cleaning & Seasoning Patch or some gun lube on a dry patch, place the patch over the cleaning jag and insert into the muzzle. Push the patch from the muzzle to the barrel shelf. This will help protect against rust and allow for easier loading. Note: As an alternative, you could use the NitroFire™ Cotton Bore Swab saturated with solvent.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Season the chamber side of the shelf
deepSteps.action: Repeat the seasoning patch from the breech opening up to the shelf.
deepSteps.quote: 10. Repeat step 9 going from the chamber. Push the patch from the breech opening to the barrel shelf. This will help protect against rust and allow for easier loading.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Clean inside the frame
deepSteps.action: Spray the frame interior and clear fouling off the frame face and barrel catch, then dry it.
deepSteps.quote: 13. To clean the inside of the frame, lightly spray cleaning solvent on the inside of the frame. Use the NitroFire™ Nylon Brush or a dry patch to remove fouling. Be sure the fouling is removed from the frame face and the barrel catch. Use a dry patch to remove any residual moisture.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38

deepSteps.title: Expose and clean the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Hold the trigger and push the hammer forward to expose the pin, clean it, then let the hammer return to rest.
deepSteps.caution: Ease the hammer down under thumb control — a dropped hammer on an empty breech is a dry fire.
deepSteps.quote: 14. Pull the trigger and push the hammer forward so the firing pin is exposed. Use a dry patch that has been sprayed with solvent to clean the exposed portion of the firing pin. After the firing pin has been cleaned, release the trigger and remove your thumb from the hammer. The hammer should move into the At Rest position and the firing pin should recess back into the frame.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38

deepSteps.title: Clean the outside of the frame
deepSteps.action: Solvent and nylon-brush the frame exterior, release lever, hammer and hammer channel.
deepSteps.quote: 15. To clean the outside of the frame, lightly spray it with solvent. Use the NitroFire™ Nylon Brush to remove any fouling from the outside of the frame, the barrel release lever, hammer, hammer extension, and inside the hammer channel.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38

deepSteps.title: Oil and grease the frame
deepSteps.action: Oil all metal inside and out, then lightly grease the pivot points.
deepSteps.quote: 16. Oil the inside and outside of the frame. Be sure to oil all metal surfaces. 17. Lightly grease the pivot points on the frame.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS™ NITROFIRE™ — FIT-75 Rev. 2 07/20 AKH — Section 17 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning, & Reassembly — p.38

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Solvent-soak the bore for 15 minutes before scrubbing
Bronze-brush breech to muzzle — the brush is the only tool that crosses the shelf
Dry-patch from the muzzle to the shelf, and stop there
Dry-patch from the breech opening to the shelf, and stop there
Seasoning or lubed patch from both directions, to the shelf

cleaning.name: Chamber and shelf
tasks: Nylon chamber brush in to the back of the shelf and out
Repeat until the chamber and the shelf's back face are clean
Confirm both faces of the shelf are clean so the Firestick seats fully

cleaning.name: Frame
tasks: Solvent and brush the frame interior, frame face and barrel catch
Clean the exposed firing pin, then let the hammer return to rest
Solvent and nylon-brush the exterior, release lever, hammer and hammer channel
Oil all metal surfaces inside and out
Light grease on the pivot points

reassembly: Press the barrel catch lever in, reinstall the barrel assembly onto the frame and lock it into place.
Reinstall the forend onto the barreled action and run the forend screw back in with the 4mm Allen wrench — do not overtighten.
fncheck: Confirm the barrel locks up on the frame, the safety moves between red-showing and no-red, and the hammer cycles to At Rest under control. Check a Firestick seats fully before you count the rifle ready — a shelf still carrying fouling is what stops it. Do not fire with excess grease or oil in the bore.
